title: Pratyahara — the senses follow the mind home (2.54–2.55)
hook: the fifth limb: when the mind settles, the senses settle with it, like bees following their leader home

segments.voice: Yesterday: pranayama. The breath grows long and subtle, and the veil over the light thins.

Try to stop hearing the fridge hum. Really try. Clench, focus, tell your ears to quit. It gets louder. Now remember the last time you were lost in a great book or a deep conversation. The fridge was humming then too. You didn't hear it. Nobody told your ears to stop. Your attention went somewhere, and your ears simply followed it. Patanjali's answer to the noisy senses isn't to fight them. It's to move the mind, and let the senses follow.
screen: `TRY NOT TO HEAR THE FRIDGE.` → `IT GETS LOUDER.` → `LOST IN A BOOK, IT'S GONE.`

segments.voice: Prati means back, toward. Ahara means taking in, even food. Pratyahara: drawing back, withdrawal. Sutra 2.54: when the senses aren't joined to their objects, they take on, as it were, the nature of the mind itself. The classical commentary gives the picture. A swarm of bees follows its leader, which the commentary calls the king of the bees. When the leader flies up, they all fly up. When it settles, they all settle. So with the senses and the mind. Restrain the mind, and the senses come home on their own. You don't chase each bee. Sutra 2.55: from this, supreme mastery of the senses. The commentary lists other views, enjoying only what's allowed, or using the senses without being hooked, and then says the highest is this: when the mind is one-pointed, the senses don't go out at all. The Bhagavad Gita has a neighbor image, the tortoise drawing its limbs into its shell. Pratyahara is the hinge of the eight. The first five limbs face outward: others, yourself, body, breath, senses. The last three face inward. And book two ends here. Look at its road: kriya yoga, discipline, study, surrender. The five afflictions, from not seeing to the fear of death. Karma's storehouse. Suffering, its cause, and its cure, discernment. Then the outer limbs, one by one. All of it, a way of calling the bees home.
screen: `PRATI-AHARA: DRAWING BACK.` · `THE BEES FOLLOW THEIR LEADER.` · `MIND SETTLES, SENSES SETTLE.` · `THE HINGE OF THE EIGHT LIMBS.` · then, large: `WITHDRAWAL.`

segments.voice: Give the mind one place to rest: the feeling of the breath at the tip of the nose. Don't try to block sounds or sights; when a noise pulls you, just return to the breath. Notice whether the hearing quiets a little on its own, following the mind.
Pratyahara. The drawing back of the senses, the fifth limb: when the mind settles, the senses follow it home.
Your line: withdrawal. Settle the leader, and the swarm comes home. Day four sixty-four, done.

howItsDone: In yoga practice, pratyahara is usually cultivated by resting attention on one object, such as the breath or a mantra, until the senses quiet; teachers often cite the Gita's tortoise drawing in its limbs as the classic image.

original.note: Sanskrit pratyāhāra: prati (back) plus āhāra (taking in); the withdrawal of the senses, the fifth limb.
